items.title: Rebuild Missing Files: don't flag a Vortex-Ghosted file as missing
items.why: A file Vortex disabled (renamed to .ghost, not deleted) is real and present -- the scan currently doesn't check for the .ghost sibling and reports it as missing. This app already has a real Ghost-awareness primitive (lib/ghost-files.js) used by Rebuild Collection; Missing Files needs the same check.
items.prompt:
REAL BUG, director-confirmed live with screenshots: Rebuild Missing Files reports a file as missing when it's actually present but Vortex-disabled (a ".ghost" file) -- confirmed case: "TGC Winterhold - ELFX Patch.esp" shows as Vortex's own "Ghost" status (screenshot of the mod list) and the real file on disk is genuinely there as "TGC Winterhold - ELFX Patch.esp.ghost" (screenshot of the staging folder) -- yet the scan flags it as "1 missing."

ROOT CAUSE: `lib/missing-files-scan.js`'s own existence check (~line 189) does a plain `fs.existsSync(path.join(action.stagingModDir, f.destination))` -- it never considers a `.ghost`-suffixed sibling as "present." This app already has a real, established Ghost-awareness primitive for exactly this concept -- `lib/ghost-files.js`'s `GHOST_SUFFIX` constant (and the reasoning in that file's own header: Vortex renames a disabled file to `<name>.ghost` rather than deleting it -- present-but-disabled, not missing) -- already used by Rebuild Collection's own `lib/rebuild-mod.js`. Reuse `GHOST_SUFFIX` from `lib/ghost-files.js` directly, don't hardcode `.ghost` again or invent new logic.

FIX: at the existence-check site (~line 189), a file counts as present if EITHER the plain destination path exists OR `<destination>.ghost` exists (case-insensitive, matching this project's own established NTFS-case-preservation convention -- see `lib/ghost-files.js`'s own comment on this). A ghosted file should NOT be flagged as missing, and should NOT be extracted/restored by Extract from Archive either (it's already there, just disabled -- re-extracting it would silently un-ghost Vortex's own disable choice, exactly the corruption `ghost-files.js`'s own header describes for Rebuild Collection's parallel case).

SCOPE CHECK: also check whether Rebuild Collection itself (the actual rebuild path, not just the diff-manifest logic already Ghost-aware via `stripGhostPairs`) has any OTHER place that could double-count a ghosted file as missing/different outside of what `ghost-files.js` already covers -- the director's own report says "this probably goes for Rebuild Collection too," so confirm live whether Rebuild Collection already handles this correctly end-to-end (it likely does, via the existing `stripGhostPairs`/`applyGhostPreservation` flow) or whether there's a real gap there too. Don't assume either way -- check.

VERIFY LIVE against the real repro: "TGC Winterhold - ELFX Patch.esp" in whichever real collection has it ghosted -- confirm it no longer shows as missing after this fix. Also confirm a GENUINELY missing file (no plain AND no `.ghost` version present) still correctly shows as missing -- don't accidentally make everything look present. Handoff with what you tested, including the Rebuild Collection scope-check finding.

items.title: Add a mod exception list -- skip hand-pick-only mods in Rebuild Collection and Rebuild Missing Files
items.why: Some mods (confirmed real: 1DustAdeptArmorSE) are hand-pick-only installers where auto-extracting the full archive installs content the user never chose, causing missing masters or crashes. Rare but destructive when it happens -- both tools need a way to skip a specific mod from automated fixing entirely, reusing the same exclude-list pattern Vortex Scrub already has.
items.prompt:
REAL FEATURE, director's own live example: some mods are hand-pick-only installers (FOMOD or similar) where the user deliberately chooses a SUBSET of what the archive contains -- confirmed real case, "1DustAdeptArmorSE" (a body-swap mod, screenshot shows 27 files reported "missing"). Auto-extracting/auto-rebuilding the FULL archive for a mod like this doesn't restore what's missing -- it installs content the user never chose, causing missing masters or crashes. Rare, but real and destructive when it happens. Both Rebuild Collection and Rebuild Missing Files need a way to SKIP a specific mod from automated fix/rebuild entirely -- an exception list, director's own term.

REUSE THE ESTABLISHED PATTERN: this app already has exactly this shape of feature -- Vortex Scrub's own exclude list (`lib/cleanup-exclude-store.js`, a simple `{staging: [], archives: []}` JSON list, load/save against a user-chosen folder, managed via a Settings section). Don't invent a new list-management UI pattern; mirror that one's shape and the general 'add/view/remove an exclusion' interaction, adapted for mod names instead of staging-folder/archive paths.

REAL DESIGN QUESTION TO RESOLVE, don't guess blind: what IDENTIFIES a mod in this list? The same mod can appear across MULTIPLE different collections (confirmed in the director's own screenshot -- several different '...Patch Collection' entries referencing similar ELFX-pattern mods) -- the exception needs to apply to that mod wherever it shows up, not just within one collection. Two real options: (a) match by mod NAME (simple, human-manageable, matches how the report already displays mods) -- risk: two genuinely different mods could share a display name; (b) match by the mod's own SOURCE identity (`identityKeys()`/`makeIdentityMatcher` from `vortex-sync/lib.js` -- the SAME cross-shape identity-matching primitive already reused for the Ignored-mods feature) -- more precise, but ties the exception to one specific archive version, so an updated version of the same mod wouldn't automatically stay excepted. Investigate which fits this use case better before building -- lean toward whichever the director's own real use case needs (a persistent "always skip this mod, however it shows up" vs. "skip this exact archive/version"), and flag your reasoning in the handoff rather than picking silently.

SCOPE:
1. New shared `lib/` module (a mod-exception-list store, mirroring `cleanup-exclude-store.js`'s own load/save shape) -- SHARED between Rebuild Collection and Rebuild Missing Files, not duplicated per-tool, since the whole point is one list both tools respect.
2. Rebuild Missing Files: a way to add a mod to the exception list directly from the scan report row (a real action, e.g. next to Extract from Archive/Download Archive) -- once excepted, that mod should show a distinct, clearly-labeled status (reuse the existing acknowledged/soft severity tier -- `--neutral`/`--neutral-bg`, action buttons suppressed -- same visual language already established for Ignored mods, DESIGN.md's own fifth tier) rather than continuing to show as a normal 'missing' problem row.
3. Rebuild Collection: excepted mods should be skipped during the actual rebuild/extraction step -- investigate the real integration point (likely `classifyMod`/`lib/rebuild-mod.js`'s own per-mod classification, similar to how `SKIP_NO_ARCHIVE`/`SKIP_OPEN_FOMOD` already exist as real skip states) and add exception as a new, similarly-real skip reason rather than a bolt-on check somewhere else.
4. A new **Reports sub-tab** (director's own correction, 2026-08-15 -- a report, not a Settings section) listing every currently-excepted mod, with the ability to add and remove entries right there. Match the EXISTING Reports pattern exactly -- same sub-nav convention as Stats/Work Through/Update Compare/Rules Generator/Workshop Report (`web/public/index.html`'s `area-reports` section, `reports-sub-*` button + `reports-sub-area-*` div), same `plan-table`/`.summary-badges` markup this app already uses everywhere else. Don't build a Settings-page list instead of a report -- the director specifically wants this visible alongside the other reports.
   **Add its Home page card in the SAME change, not a follow-up** -- every existing Reports sub-tab has its own card in `web/public/index.html`'s home-card grid (`data-section="homeSectionReports"`); add this one's there too, don't leave it only reachable via the Reports sub-nav.

VERIFY LIVE against the real repro mod ("1DustAdeptArmorSE" or an equivalent hand-pick-only mod) -- add it to the exception list from the Missing Files report, confirm it shows the new excepted status and no longer offers Extract from Archive, confirm Rebuild Collection also skips it correctly on a real rebuild run, and confirm removing it from Settings restores normal behavior. Handoff with what you tested and which identity-matching approach you went with and why.
